label: assumption (Birdbrain estimate, second edition)
rationale: Indexing and explorer code is commodity that agents write and maintain. Archive nodes, storage and bandwidth stay, which is why the labour share is lower.

label: assumption (Birdbrain estimate, second edition)
rationale: Interfaces are close to free to produce. Key handling, signing review and app-store release are what remain, and a small team carries them.

label: assumption (Birdbrain estimate, second edition)
rationale: Libraries, CLIs, type generation and docs are where agents are strongest, generated against the chain's own metadata. API design stays.

label: assumption (Birdbrain estimate, second edition)
rationale: Agents now write and test most protocol code. Review, research and formal reasoning still set the pace, and a fault costs the network, so this falls least among software.

label: assumption (Birdbrain estimate, second edition)
rationale: Mostly hardware, bandwidth and on-call. Automation removes most of the operating labour, not the machines.

label: assumption (Birdbrain estimate, second edition)
rationale: Machine review finds more for far less. A named reviewer still has to sign and carry liability.

label: assumption (Birdbrain estimate, second edition)
rationale: Literature, data work and drafting collapse. Choosing the question and standing behind the answer do not.

label: assumption (Birdbrain estimate, second edition)
rationale: Course material and translation are near free. Venues, travel and stipends are not.

label: assumption (Birdbrain estimate, second edition)
rationale: Agency and content-production fees collapse to a few people with agents. Sponsorships and paid media are bought, not built.

label: assumption (Birdbrain estimate, second edition)
rationale: Venues, flights and people in rooms. Organising labour shrinks.

label: assumption (Birdbrain estimate, second edition)
rationale: Integration work gets cheap; relationships, deals and the choice of whom to back do not.

label: assumption (Birdbrain estimate, second edition)
rationale: Grantees build far faster, so the same output costs much less. Selection is unchanged.

label: assumption (Birdbrain estimate, second edition)
rationale: Drafting and reconciliation are largely automated; accountability and entity costs remain.

rationale: Capital, not labour. Agents do not make a liquidity programme cheaper, only the decision about whether to run it.
